inspiration: Planet-wide landmark pointer: one cached list of every named place on the planet, fetched once and then queried many times. Filter by category, drop inactive places, then sort nearest-first with an optional radius cap (map.ts lines 6, 226-232). For us this is a minimap or waypoint pointer to shrines, chests or the Pit gate in any zone. Keep the cache-once shape; change the source to our zone data.

Hub categories as a small fixed table of about twelve named categories with stable numeric ids (map.ts lines 39-51): bank, cantina, starport, medical centre, cloning, hotel, guild, city and others. Idea for our zones: a fixed hub-type list (camp, shrine, gate, market) as zone data fields rather than free text.

Friendly-name aliases sit in front of the canonical category table, so 'hospital' resolves to 'medicalcenter' (map.ts lines 58-64). Good for authoring: accept common words in content files, store one canonical key.

Golden pin test: the category index table is locked by a unit test so a data-table bump fails CI instead of silently shifting ids (map.ts line 19). Matches our catalogue-as-runtime-source row 20: a data change must fail a test, not drift.

Versioned binary headers fail loudly: the STF reader checks a fixed magic before trusting any entry (stf-reader.ts lines 71-72). Apply the same idea to any binary catalogue we ship: check magic and version, refuse on mismatch.

Golden binary fixtures per format (one object template, one portal layout, one login packet dump) make the parsers testable without the live server. Idea for our zone layout files: keep one small fixture per zone format.

briefs.label: Nearest-landmark pointer (own label: Waypoint Beacon)
briefs.why: A single cached list of places, filtered and sorted by distance, gives a clear pointer at any range. The pointer is a readable cue at 375 wide because only the nearest one is shown.
briefs.keep: cache once per zone; filter by category; nearest first; optional radius; inactive places hidden
briefs.change: our pointer colours by threat or quest state, not by a category id; it is drawn as a ground ring plus a short bearing tick, not a text row; the source is zone data, not a server list

briefs.label: Hub-type zone tag set (own label: Hub Tags)
briefs.why: About twelve stable hub tags make a zone readable at a glance: each hub has one tag and one icon family.
briefs.keep: small fixed tag list with stable ids; one tag per hub; ids never reused
briefs.change: our tags are camp, shrine, gate, market and pit, with our own names and icons; no copy of the donor's category names or ids
